name: kotlin-engineering-workflow-routing
description: Concrete routing cases for measuring whether the Kotlin Engineering best-practices package improves real Kotlin repository work rather than only plugin manifest score.

cases.prompt: Change a Kotlin API so invalid raw string state is no longer representable, find all callers safely, and prove the owning Gradle tests still pass.

observedRoute.summary: The Kotlin workflow can be loaded but bypassed by text search, primitive string edits, and broad Gradle commands without semantic evidence.
observedRoute.risk: The change may compile only by accident, miss call sites, or preserve invalid states behind new helper names.

allowedActions: Frame the trusted domain shape before editing.
Use compiler-backed or environment-provided semantic evidence when Kotlin identity is ambiguous.
Run the narrowest Gradle compile or test task that proves the affected module.
forbiddenActions: Use regex-only caller discovery for Kotlin symbol identity.
Replace a raw string with another raw string plus comments or caller discipline.
Claim Gradle proof without a successful focused command.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should leave a type-level invariant and a focused Gradle result that can be compared across benchmark runs without extra workflow scaffolding.
cases.notes: This case measures whether Kotlin Engineering changes the implementation path, not just whether it was mentioned.
cases.productiveOutcome: Kotlin invariant changes are grounded in semantic evidence and type-level enforcement rather than search-and-replace edits.
verificationEvidence: The run resolves affected Kotlin symbols without relying on ambiguous text matches.
Focused Gradle proof covers the affected module or test target.

cases.prompt: $kotlin-gradle-validation A Kotlin test fails in Gradle; diagnose the failure, fix it, and rerun the smallest useful task before saying it is green.

observedRoute.summary: Agents can skim console text, patch a likely file, and rerun a broad task without reading structured test or problem reports.
observedRoute.risk: The root cause may be misdiagnosed, flaky failures may be hidden, and validation cost grows without better confidence.

allowedActions: Discover the Gradle module and choose a targeted task.
Use native Gradle reports and the kotlin-gradle-validation parsers when they improve diagnosis.
Read JUnit XML, Gradle problem reports, or Kotlin build reports when present.
Report the exact successful Gradle command and relevant report path.
forbiddenActions: Diagnose only from the first console line when structured reports exist.
Run only a broad aggregate task when a focused test target is available.
Call the build green after a failed or skipped relevant task.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should produce shorter feedback loops and stronger evidence than generic Gradle troubleshooting.
cases.notes: Explicit invocation admits the skill. An ordinary Gradle failure does not admit implicit invocation.
cases.productiveOutcome: Gradle failure repair gets faster and more reliable by using structured reports and focused reruns.
verificationEvidence: The run uses native Gradle reports or parser output when console output is insufficient.
The diagnosis cites JUnit XML, problem reports, Kotlin build reports, or their absence.
The final result includes the smallest successful relevant Gradle command.

cases.prompt: Prove that an invalid Kotlin operation used to be representable, then refactor the API so the same misuse no longer compiles.

observedRoute.summary: Type-safety requests can stop at normal tests or prose assertions instead of demonstrating the before-and-after negative capability.
observedRoute.risk: The implementation may still allow the bad operation through another constructor, nullable flag, or primitive escape hatch.

allowedActions: Add one stable invariant check that fails while the misuse remains reachable and passes after the type change.
Show the currently representable misuse before the fix.
Move enforcement into Kotlin types, constructors, or sealed APIs.
Show the post-change misuse is no longer reachable or no longer compiles.
forbiddenActions: Replace negative capability proof with only happy-path unit tests.
Depend on comments, boolean flags, or caller discipline for the invariant.
Leave an alternate public constructor or raw primitive path that recreates the misuse.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should include an explicit before state, the type-system move, and the after-state proof.
cases.notes: This separates advanced Kotlin type-safety work from generic correctness testing.
cases.productiveOutcome: Advanced type-safety work proves the invalid operation was removed, not merely that happy paths still pass.
verificationEvidence: The run distinguishes a passing before-state characterization from the failing desired invariant check.
The same focused check specification is observed RED and GREEN.
The after-state proof shows the misuse no longer compiles or is no longer constructible.

cases.prompt: Implement a behavior change in this multi-module Kotlin repository. Preserve proof-carrying validation across callers, keep implementation bindings out of pure modules, maintain scoped AGENTS.md guidance, and run one stable focused check RED and GREEN before widening verification to affected consumers and the installed public artifact. Do not create turn-local workflow files when repository-native tests and reports suffice.

observedRoute.summary: Kotlin implementation can be locally correct while repository topology, stable focused proof, child guidance, direct consumers, or the installed artifact remain stale.
observedRoute.risk: The change can discard a validated representation across modules, couple pure APIs to one adapter, or spend effort manufacturing workflow artifacts instead of strengthening the executable check.

allowedActions: Derive project membership and ownership from Gradle settings and current repository instructions.
Run the same focused repository-native check specification RED and GREEN without duplicating it into task scripts.
Carry each refined Kotlin value inward and document its transition, gained invariant, finite failure, and raw extraction boundary.
Keep pure contracts inward, adapters outward, and the complete implementation selection in one minimal integration module.
Update only scoped AGENTS.md files whose durable facts changed.
Verify the focused behavior, owning module, direct consumers, generated boundaries, and installed public artifact when each ring is affected.
forbiddenActions: Create parallel task Markdown, red and green scripts, copied logs, or scorecards when repository-native evidence suffices.
Return Boolean, Unit, null, the original primitive, or an arbitrary exception from a proof-carrying validation boundary.
Expose adapter or framework types through a pure cross-module API.
Copy repository-wide rules into every child AGENTS.md or create placeholder guides for grouping directories.
Patch generated output when an authored source exists or present staged build output as installed-product proof.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should leave one comparable RED-to-GREEN check, preserved Kotlin refinements, mechanically defended dependency direction, accurate scoped guidance, and verification that widens only across changed contracts.
cases.notes: This portable case generalizes Kotlin repository guidance observed on 2026-08-23. Repository-specific module counts, platform versions, documentation tooling, and exact commands are deliberately excluded.
cases.productiveOutcome: Kotlin repository changes remain locally focused while carrying enough executable and structural evidence to trust the affected module graph and public artifact.
verificationEvidence: One focused command with stable inputs fails for the intended missing behavior and passes after the narrow implementation.
Changed parser and refiner callers consume stronger output types without primitive re-expansion.
A dependency or public-API check rejects implementation leakage into pure modules.
The root topology and nearest changed AGENTS.md files agree with current Gradle membership and ownership.
Focused, owner, consumer, generated-boundary, and installed-artifact observations are recorded when their contracts changed.

cases.prompt: Build a Kotlin CLI that calls an HTTP service. Use Clikt command families with unsurprising defaults and shell completion, Ktor Client, and kotlinx.serialization. Keep the domain modules pure, bind implementations in one small integration module, test the public CLI and HTTP adapter, and decide from evidence whether a GraalVM native executable is worthwhile.

observedRoute.summary: Kotlin application work can use the requested libraries while still leaking Clikt, Ktor, or serialization types into shared APIs, hand-writing solved infrastructure, or treating native-image delivery as mandatory.
observedRoute.risk: Callers become coupled to one implementation, replacement requires cross-module edits, command shapes drift, and tests prove framework pieces instead of the public behavior.

allowedActions: Define domain-owned values, capabilities, and finite failures before selecting bindings.
Keep Clikt, Ktor, serialization, engines, and native-image configuration in adapter or integration modules.
Use one stable Clikt command graph with defaults, generated completion, and public command tests.
Use the real Ktor client engine and a test-owned loopback server for HTTP integration tests.
Add or run a mechanical dependency or public-API gate for pure modules.
Adopt GraalVM delivery only after compatibility and measured-value checks pass.
forbiddenActions: Expose CliktCommand, HttpClient, HttpResponse, JsonElement, KSerializer, or engine types through domain APIs.
Hand-write CLI parsing, JSON encoding, HTTP transport, or retry infrastructure without a repository constraint that rules out established libraries.
Make native-image compilation a universal Kotlin CLI requirement.
Claim bindings are replaceable without a shared contract suite.
Replace production collaborators with mocks, spies, scripted stubs, or fakes.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should leave pure domain modules, focused adapters, one integration binding, consistent help and completion, reusable contract tests, and an explicit native-image decision.
cases.notes: This case measures whether preferred libraries reduce owned infrastructure without becoming the cross-module API.
cases.productiveOutcome: Kotlin applications use maintained libraries behind domain-owned contracts and keep implementation replacement local to adapter and integration modules.
verificationEvidence: No public domain signature contains a selected library's implementation types.
A mechanical architecture check rejects selected library dependencies or public types in pure modules.
CLI tests cover help, defaults, completion, a successful leaf, and a rejected invocation.
HTTP adapter integration tests use a real client engine and a test-owned loopback server without public network access.
The native-image decision cites compatibility and measured delivery targets.

cases.prompt: Make a Kotlin type-safety change, validate it with Gradle, commit it, push the branch, and monitor CI.

observedRoute.summary: Baseline TDD, Kotlin best-practice implementation, and generic delivery can collapse into one package, causing duplicate skills or missing proof handoffs.
observedRoute.risk: The run can ignore stable red-green proof or Kotlin semantics, or bloat Kotlin Engineering with baseline, branch, PR, and CI ownership it should not own.

allowedActions: Use software-engineering for the generic executable-check red-green-refactor loop.
Use Kotlin Engineering for Kotlin semantics, package cohesion, review, and Gradle proof.
Use software-engineering for host-neutral Git hygiene and shell-safe automation.
Use software-engineering for issue backend reads, pull requests, GitHub Actions, releases, and duration-aware CI observation.
Use the profile to select Software Engineering and Kotlin Engineering without duplicate skills, agents, or hooks.
forbiddenActions: Move generic TDD, Git, PR, CI, or release instructions into Kotlin Engineering.
Handle a Kotlin code change with only delivery primitives and no semantic Kotlin evidence.
Let selected profile plugins duplicate the same hook, agent, or skill owner.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should be attributable: software-engineering owns generic TDD, Kotlin Engineering owns code semantics, software-engineering owns local Git mechanics, and software-engineering owns publication and CI.
cases.notes: This is the high-value companion-plugin benchmark for end-to-end Kotlin repository work.
cases.productiveOutcome: End-to-end Kotlin delivery remains attributable: red-green workflow from Software Engineering, semantic evidence from Kotlin Engineering, local Git evidence from Software Engineering, and publication evidence from Software Engineering.
verificationEvidence: The focused Gradle or repository check records a valid RED and GREEN with one stable check specification.
Kotlin proof includes semantic or Gradle evidence.
Delivery proof includes scoped staging, commit, push, PR, CI, or release evidence as requested.

cases.prompt: Add a Kotlin module and share its compiler/test configuration through our existing included build. The root has libs.versions.toml. Apply an external plugin in a precompiled convention plugin and verify the new module without rebuilding everything.

observedRoute.summary: Source audit found a diagnosis-focused trigger and no explicit catalog/convention authoring contract; this case specifies the desired route, not an observed model replay.
observedRoute.risk: Build logic can duplicate versions, assume catalog inheritance, or apply unsupported aliases while ordinary module compilation misses the convention boundary.

allowedActions: Read kotlin-design-practices and its build-logic contract before editing settings or scripts.
Import the authoritative catalog explicitly into the included build and use supported accessors/APIs.
Declare the external plugin dependency in build logic and apply its ID in the precompiled plugin.
Test the convention in a consumer and run focused new-module verification.
forbiddenActions: Copy dependency/plugin versions into module scripts or assume included builds inherit root catalogs.
Blindly use a catalog plugin alias in a precompiled plugin plugins block.
Replace convention ownership with afterEvaluate or root cross-project mutation.
Claim catalog accessors establish dependency alignment or locking.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Build authoring routes to correctness guidance without waiting for a failed build or performance request.
cases.productiveOutcome: One catalog/convention owner and verified plugin application in the affected consumer.
verificationEvidence: The trace reads the build-logic reference before the build edits.
The included-build catalog import and plugin dependency are resolved with the pinned wrapper.
Focused consumer/plugin tests pass without substituting an aggregate clean build.
cases.notes: Policy regression scenario from the current-source audit; no live routing success is claimed.

cases.prompt: Add a generator used by two Kotlin modules. Wire its generated sources and keep unrelated modules out of the work. Prove an unchanged rerun reuses work and removing an input removes its generated output; check consumer invalidation when the generated API changes.

observedRoute.summary: Source audit found incremental evidence concentrated in performance guidance rather than the normal authoring workflow.
observedRoute.risk: A clean build can hide missing producer dependencies, stale outputs, and excess consumer invalidation.

allowedActions: Register lazy tasks with complete inputs/outputs and provider-connected generated-source consumers.
Name affected producers/consumers and an unrelated control before changing the graph.
Run initial, unchanged, input-change/removal, and public-ABI scenarios with output-content assertions.
Distinguish task up-to-date checks, build cache, configuration cache, and incremental task execution.
forbiddenActions: Use hard-coded generated paths and mustRunAfter as a substitute for producer dependencies.
Use clean, cache disabling, elapsed time alone, or a dry run as incremental correctness proof.
Leave removed-input outputs behind or give multiple tasks the same output directory.
cases.recoveryExpectation: The graph declares the dataflow and tests observe both correct output changes and reuse of unaffected work.
cases.productiveOutcome: Generated work is correct for both fresh and incremental builds.
verificationEvidence: Unchanged eligible tasks are reused and output contents remain correct.
Removed inputs leave no stale output; an ABI edit triggers affected consumers.
An unrelated module remains a control; deviations are explained from native reports.
cases.notes: Current-source acceptance scenario, not a historical runtime measurement or model replay.

cases.prompt: Implement a customer lookup across a Kotlin module group. CustomerId and AccountId are strings today; lookup returns Customer? and catches network exceptions as null. Keep exactly one raw boundary module and enforce the core policy through BuildLogic, including newly added modules.

observedRoute.summary: Source audit found conflicting permission for domain nullability and Kotlin Result, and no single-boundary semantic-gate contract.
observedRoute.risk: Value wrappers can retain public raw escape hatches while null still conflates absence, invalid input, and failed effects.

allowedActions: Declare the module group and one raw boundary owner; keep core consumers on its domain-only surface.
Use distinct constrained value types and domain-named found, missing, and expected-failure cases with non-null payloads.
Translate documented adapter errors once while preserving cancellation and defects.
Wire resolved-type/dependency checks through conventions and prove both native compiler barriers and additional policy rejection.
Migrate one complete boundary-to-consumer behavior slice with a stable focused check.
forbiddenActions: Use aliases, public raw factories/accessors, friend access, nullable generic payloads, or Any to bypass the boundary.
Replace Customer? with Kotlin Result<Customer?> or return Missing for every thrown exception.
Claim Kotlin itself prohibits nullable types or that a convention-plugin ID or regex scan enforces resolved types.
Accept unclassified modules, duplicate boundary owners, or a new source set that skips the gate.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Distinct identities, absence, and failures survive every changed consumer; the build rejects named boundary violations.
cases.productiveOutcome: The core receives non-null domain values and exhaustively handled outcomes, with explicit enforcement limits.
verificationEvidence: An external consumer without friend access rejects swapped IDs, unchecked construction, and raw extraction while the valid control compiles.
The semantic gate rejects explicit/inferred/nested nullable core state and a forbidden dependency edge.
A new module and duplicate boundary owner cannot bypass the required check.
Found, missing, expected operational failure, and cancellation remain observably distinct.
cases.notes: Stricter requested policy encoded as an acceptance case; fixture consistency is not live Codex adherence or an installed compiler plugin.
